title: Isolation of Next-Generation Gene Therapy Vectors through Engineering, Barcoding, and Screening of Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV) Capsid Variants
protocol: Order the degenerate oligonucleotides to avoid codon bias.
Design the amplification primer: 5' CTCGTCAGCCGCCTGG 3'.
Resuspend both the degenerate oligonucleotides and amplification primer in TE buffer to a final concentration of 100 µM.

Set up a PCR reaction with 1 µL of each primer, 10 µL of buffer, 1.5 µL of DMSO, 0.5 µL of dNTPs (10 mM), 0.5 µL of Hi-fidelity Hot Start Polymerase II, and 35.5 µL of nuclease-free water in a total volume of 50 µL.
Convert the synthesized single-stranded DNA to double-stranded DNA.
Digest the PCR product with appropriate restriction enzymes.
Ligate the digested PCR product to an acceptor plasmid.
Electroporate the ligated mixture into competent cells.
Transfer the reaction to a thermocycler.
Run a pre-incubation step for 10 seconds at 98 °C.
Cycle three times: incubate for 10 s at 98 °C, then 30 s at 59 °C, and finally 10 s at 72 °C.
Incubate for 5 min at 72 °C.
Cool the reaction down.
Purify the reaction using a nucleotide removal kit.
Elute in 100 μL of nuclease-free water.
Digest 85 µL of the purified insert with 10 µL of 10x buffer and 5 µL of BglI enzyme in a final 100 µL reaction volume.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Purify using a nucleotide removal kit.
Elute in 50 µL of nuclease-free water.
Quantify using the type "Oligo DNA" in a spectrophotometer.
Digest 10 µg of a replication-competent AAV plasmid with 20 µL of 10x buffer and 10 µL of SfiI enzyme in a final 200 µL reaction volume.
Incubate at 50 °C overnight.
Purify the vector on a 1% agarose gel using the gel extraction kit.
Quantify the concentration in a spectrophotometer.
Ligate 955 ng of plasmid vector with 45 ng of insert using 2 µL of buffer and 2 µL of ligase in a 20 µL ligation reaction.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16 °C overnight.
Heat-inactivate the ligase by incubating the reaction at 70 °C for 10 minutes.
Purify the ligation reaction using a DNA purifying kit following the manufacturer's instructions.
Elute the purified reaction in approximately 80% of the starting volume of nuclease-free water and store on ice for transformation.
Thaw one vial of electrocompetent cells on ice for 10 minutes.
Add 1-2 µL of the purified ligation reaction to 30 µL of electrocompetent cells and mix by gently tapping.
Transfer the cell/DNA mixture carefully into a pre-chilled 1 mm gap electroporation cuvette without introducing air bubbles.
Electroporate using settings: 1800 V, 600 Ω, and 10 µF.
Immediately after electroporation, add 970 µL of pre-warmed recovery media to the cuvette and mix by pipetting.
Transfer the cell/recovery media mixture to a micro centrifuge tube.
Incubate the cells for 1 hour at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Repeat reactions 10-100 times as desired to achieve diversity.
Pool all reaction tubes after incubation into one single tube.
Dilute 10 µL of the pooled transformations in PBS at 10-, 100-, or 1,000-fold dilutions.
Spread 100 μL on nutrient agar plates containing 75 mg/mL of ampicillin.
Incubate agar plates overnight at 37 °C.
Count colonies on the agar plates.
Calculate theoretical maximal diversity using the formula: 10 x dilution factor x number of colonies x number of electroporation reactions.
Sequence at least 20 colonies by Sanger sequencing to confirm library quality.
Inoculate 400-1,000 mL of LB medium containing the appropriate antibiotic and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 180 rpm.
Prepare a glycerol stock from the overnight culture by mixing equal volumes of bacterial culture and 50% glycerol solution in nuclease-free water.
Freeze the glycerol stock at -80 °C.
Purify the plasmid library using a plasmid maxi kit.
Transfect the plasmid library (pRep2Cap2_PI, peptide insert) together with an adeno-helper plasmid to HEK293T cells.
Use polyethylenimine (PEI) as a transfection reagent.
Collect the cells after 3 days and subject them to three cycles of freeze-thaw.
Purify the viral lysate using cesium chloride gradient ultracentrifugation.
Exchange buffer for PBS.
Concentrate the viral particles.
Serially dilute 2 µL of the AAV vector stock in 198 µL of nuclease-free water to yield a 1:106 final dilution.
Mix thoroughly each time using a 200 µL pipette.
Add one no-template control (NTC) as a negative control.
Prepare a 20x primer-probe mix by adding 3.6 µL of each of the 100 µM primers, 1 µL each of the 100 µM dd-PCR probes, and 3.6 µL of nuclease-free water to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Prepare a 22 µL PCR reaction by adding 5.5 µL of sample.
Add 1.1 µL of 20x primer-probe mix to the PCR reaction.
Mix 11 µL of dd-PCR supermix for probes (no dUTP) into the reaction.
Add 4.4 µL of nuclease-free water to complete the reaction mixture.
Generate droplets using a droplet generator.
Transfer the droplet reaction to a 96-well plate.
Place the plate into a thermocycler.
Run a denaturation step for 10 min at 94 °C.
Cycle through 40 cycles of 30 s at 94 °C and 1 min at 58 °C.
Heat-inactivate the polymerase for 10 min at 98 °C.
Add a final cooling step to the thermocycling process.
Read the reactions in a droplet reader.
Open the saved dd-PCR plate file using analysis software.
Use the threshold tool in the 1D Amplitude tab to separate negative and positive droplets for each channel, guided by the NTC.
Export data to a csv file from the analysis software.
Calculate the correction factor CF using the provided formula.
Calculate the final vector concentration c using the given equation.
Amplify the 96-nucleotide peptide insertion fragment by setting up a 20 µL PCR reaction using a proof-reading polymerase kit (2x).
Add 1 µL of AAV stock containing 1 x 108 vg to the PCR reaction.
Add 0.5 µL of each of 100 µM primer (NGS_forward and NGS_reverse) to the PCR reaction.
Adjust the final volume to 20 µL with nuclease-free water.
Transfer the reaction to a thermocycler and run a denaturation step for 3 min at 98 °C.
Run 30-35 cycles of 10 s at 98 °C, 10 s at 59 °C, and 20 s at 72 °C.
Perform a final extension for 5 min at 72 °C.
Cool the reaction down after the final cycle.
Purify the samples using a PCR purification kit.
Quantify the concentration in a spectrophotometer.
Run a 3% agarose gel to verify purity and fragment size.
Process the PCR fragments using the library system for low complexity samples kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Perform the end repair reaction with 30 ng of PCR fragment.
Ligate adaptors to the repaired ends.
Amplify the adaptor-ligated DNA for 10 cycles.
Purify the reactions using a PCR purification kit.
Process the final products on a Bioanalyzer to verify size and purity using a DNA reagents kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify the amplicons using a fluorometer.
Pool the quantified amplicons.
Quantify the final pooled NGS library again on a fluorometer (according to the manufacturer's instructions).
Verify the quality of the final pooled NGS library on a Bioanalyzer.
Sequence the NGS libraries in single-end (SE) mode, using a 75-cycle high output kit with a read length of 84 and an index 1 of 8.
Analyze the NGS sequencing data with Python 3 and biopython.
Search the sequence files for sequences that satisfy certain criteria (presence of recognition sequences flanking the insertion site) using Script#1 and a configuration file.
Extract and store the correct sequence in an output file, which is a txt file with the same name as the sequencing file.
Prepare two folders: Script and Data.
Copy the gzip-compressed sequencing result files to the Data folder.
Copy the Python files Script#1_DetectionExtraction_JoVE_Py3.py and Script#2_PV_extraction_and_ranking_Py3.py to the Script folder.
Copy the configuration file Barcode_Script_JoVE.conf to the Script folder.
Copy the Look-up table file Zuordnung.txt to the Script folder.
Edit the "Zuordnung.txt" file by adding in two tab-separated columns, the names of the gzip files and the desired final name.
Change the variable my_dir = "~/Data/" in the configuration file Barcode_Script_JoVE.conf.
Set the filename_sample_file = "~/Script/Zuordnung.txt" in the configuration file.
Use the following command to call the variant sequence detection and extraction: python3 ~/Script#1_DetectionExtraction_JoVE_Py3.py ~/Barcode_Script_JoVE.conf
Perform PV extraction and analysis using the following command: python3 ~/Script#2_PV_extraction_and_ranking_Py3.py ~/Barcode_Script_JoVE.conf
Ensure that the three output files contain statistical data.
Include "# of Valid PV reads", "# of Invalid PV reads", and "# of unique PV reads" in the first rows.
Add a first column with the index of each DNA sequence from the input txt files.
For "…analyzed_all.csv": include columns for "Sample:", "#", "Frw or Rev", and "PVs".
Label invalid sequences with "NA" and "not valid" in the last two columns.
For "…analyzed_validSeq.csv": filter for valid sequences only, based on the previous file's format.
For "…analyzed_PV.csv": include columns for "PVs", "#", and "count".
Merge frw and rev counts from the previous files to provide a single count of 1 or 2.
Visualize the output files using available software based on user needs.
Verify the functionality of identified peptide sequences and compare them with reference AAV capsids.
Insert the capsid sequence into a Rep/Cap helper construct without ITRs.
Produce barcoded AAV library for each capsid variant using the three-plasmid system.
Design 15 nucleotide long barcodes with homopolymers of less than three nucleotides and GC content below 65%.
Ensure a Hamming distance greater than four nucleotides between designed barcodes.
Produce each AAV capsid separately in combination with a transgene plasmid carrying a unique barcode.
Perform the AAV titration by replacing the Rep2 primer pair with the YFP primer pair.
Quantify individual AAV productions.
Pool equal amounts of each production to generate the final barcoded library.
Quantify the final library again to check concentration and quality.
Apply the barcoded AAV library systemically to a model system (e.g., mice).
Collect ON- and OFF-target tissues or cell types based on the experiment.
Freeze collected tissues at -80 °C.
Extract DNA and RNA from the tissues of interest using the DNA/RNA Mini Kit.
Place a small piece of tissue (1 mm3, about 5 mg) in a 2 mL reaction tube.
Add lysis buffer mixed with β-mercaptoethanol (1%) to the tissue.
Add 5 mm steel beads and homogenize the tissue in a tissueLyser for 45 s at 40 Hz.
Incubate with 10 µL of proteinase K (10 mg/mL) for 15 min at 55 °C while shaking at 400 rpm.
Centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Collect the supernatant.
Proceed with the manufacturer's protocol of the DNA/RNA Kit.
Split the washing step into two steps using 350 μL of wash buffer in each step.
Digest remnant DNA on the column with RNase-free DNase I.
Add 80 µL of the DNase I solution to the column and incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Elute RNA/DNA from the column with nuclease-free water.
Store isolated RNA at -80 °C.
Store gDNA at -20 °C.
Subject RNA samples to another round of DNase I treatment for 15-30 min before reverse-transcription reaction.
Add 1 µL of DNase I solution, 4 µL of buffer, and nuclease-free water to a final volume of 40 µL containing 212 ng of RNA.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Heat inactivate the sample at 70 °C for 10 min.
Synthesize cDNA using 150 ng of RNA according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Include controls without reverse transcriptase to ensure no contaminating viral DNA from the sample.
Store cDNA at -20 °C.
Amplify the barcode sequence using primers BC-seq forward and BC-seq reverse.
Prepare PCR master-mix under a clean PCR hood: add 0.5 µL of Hi-fidelity DNA polymerase, 10 µL of 5x buffer, 0.25 µL of each primer (BC-seq fw/BC-seq rv), and 1 µl of 10 mM dNTPs.
Adjust the final volume to 50 µL with nuclease-free water using 25 ng of cDNA or DNA/reaction as template.
Perform PCR cycling: incubate for 30 s at 98 °C, followed by 40 cycles at 98 °C for 10 s and 72 °C for 20 s, and a final 5 min step at 72 °C.
Verify the size of the PCR fragment by gel electrophoresis.
Purify the DNA using commercially available magnetic beads or column-based systems.
Prepare the NGS library using a system for low complexity samples according to manufacturer instructions.
Determine the DNA concentration via the dsDNA HS Kit.
Analyze the quality of the library as previously described.
Pool the prepared libraries.
Quantify the pooled library on a fluorometer.
Assess the quality of the pooled library on a Bioanalyzer.
Perform NGS sequencing as discussed in section 1.9.7.
Prepare a 60x primer/probe mix for EYFP (1.5 µM YFP_fw, 1.5 µM YFP_rv, and 0.6 µM YFP_probe).
Set up the qPCR reaction on ice to determine the copy number of EYFP and GAPDH.
Use a GAPDH primer/probe mix to determine the copy number of the housekeeping gene.
Prepare a PCR master mix (15 µL).
Add 60x primer/probe mix (0.5 µL) to the master mix.
Transfer 15.5 µL of the master mix into a 96-well plate.
Add 14.5 µL of sample or standard (75 ng total DNA concentration) to each well in the 96-well plate.
Seal the 96-well plate with foil.
Vortex the sealed plate.
Spin the plate briefly at high speed to ensure mixing.
Transfer 10 µL of each sample into a 384-well plate in duplicates.
Seal the 384-well plate with foil.
Spin the 384-well plate at 800 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Incubate the reaction mix in a thermocycler at 50 °C for 2 min.
Perform an initial activation step of 10 min at 95 °C.
Denature the samples at 95 °C for 15 s followed by annealing/extension at 60 °C for 1 min. Perform this cycle 40 times.
Use the GAPDH copy number to calculate the number of diploid genomes (dg) by dividing by two.
Divide the EYFP copy number by the number of dg to obtain vector genomes per diploid genome (vg/dg).
Generate the Normalization_Organ.txt file using the calculated vg/dg value for bioinformatic analysis.
Analyze NGS sequencing data following the workflow described in Weinmann et al.24.
Detect barcode sequences guided by flanking sequences, their length and location using Script#1_BarcodeDetection.py.
Analyze barcode enrichment and distribution over tissues using Script#2_BarcodeAnalysis.py.
Place archived fastq files of sequencing data in a directory named "Data_to_analyze".
Create a tab-delimited text file named "Variants.txt" with barcode sequences assigned to AAV capsid variant names.
Create another tab-delimited contamination file named "Contaminations.txt" listing barcode sequences from possible contamination sources.
Edit the configuration file "Barcode_Script.conf" to include path to folder with sequencing data.
Specify sequence of flanking regions of the barcodes in the configuration file.
Indicate position of the barcodes in the configuration file.
Set window size for barcode detection in the configuration file.
Call barcode detection using the command: python3 ~/Script#1_BarcodeDetection.py ~/Barcode_Script.conf
Execute Script#2_BarcodeAnalysis.py with txt files obtained from barcode detection run.
Assign names to each txt file in "Zuordnung.txt" corresponding to tissue/organ names.
Create an "organs.txt" text file with the list of names for ON- and OFF-target organs.
Create a "Normalization_Organ.txt" tab-delimited text file with normalized values for all capsid variants and all organs/tissues.
Write the names given for each organ in the first column of the "Normalization_Organ.txt" file.
Enter the normalization values for the corresponding tissues in the second column of the "Normalization_Organ.txt" file.
Create a "Normalization_Variant.txt" tab-delimited text file with normalized values for all capsid variants and organs/tissues.
List the names of each cap in the first column of the "Normalization_Variant.txt" file.
Enter the normalized values of read counts for each cap in the pooled library in the second column of the "Normalization_Variant.txt" file.
Edit the configuration file by specifying full paths to all additional files mentioned above.
Execute Script#2_BarcodeAnalysis.py using the specified command.
Visualize the data using the spreadsheet file that combines text file data into merged matrix data.
Perform cluster analysis of the matrix data to distinguish capsid properties and evaluate their similarities based on RC profiles across tissues.
Run the PCA_heatmap_plot.R script with the relativeconcentration.xls files as input: Rscript --vanilla ~/PCA.R ~/relativeconcentration.xls
Generate hierarchical cluster heatmap plots from the input data.
Generate principal component analysis (PCA) plots from the input data.
